newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Telekom says early equal access unlikely.
newsitem.headline: Telekom says early equal access unlikely.

text.p: Telekom Malaysia Bhd's chief executive Mohamed Said Mohamed Ali said on Thursday he did not think an industry deadline on "equal access" would be brought forward.
"I don't think the deadline for equal access will be moved up," he told reporters at a news conference after releasing the company's 1996's financial results.
When asked why he thought the deadline would not be brought earlier, he said, "I can't say."
He added however, that he did not think the telecommunications industry was ready for equal access at the moment.

Equal access implies that all of state telecommunications firm Telekom's three million subscribers would be able to use alternative networks of its Malaysian competitors in making international and long-distance domestic calls.
Speculation in recent weeks that the date of implementation on January 1, 1999 may be brought forward has depressed Telekom's stock.
